title: Chain rule for conditional mutual information
statement:
Let $X$, $W$, $Y$, and $Z$ be random variables on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$, each valued in a countable measurable space and each attaining only finitely many values, and suppose $\mu$ is either the zero measure or a probability measure. Writing $I[U : V \mid T;\mu]$ for the mutual information of $U$ and $V$ conditioned on $T$, the pair $(X,W)$ obeys the chain rule
\[
  I[(X,W) : Y \mid Z;\mu]
  \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;+\; I[W : Y \mid (X,Z);\mu].
\]
hypotheses_covered: X, W, Y, Z are measurable
each of X, W, Y, Z has finite range
μ is zero or a probability measure
value spaces are countable with measurable singletons
replaced:
For measurable $X$, $W$, $Y$, $Z$ with finite ranges under a zero-or-probability measure,
\[
  I[(X,W) : Y \mid Z;\mu]
  \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;+\; I[W : Y \mid (X, Z);\mu].
\]
